bibl.title: 无骨者伊瓦尔《战国历史地图·年表》

div.head: Shiji I: Basic Annals
div.p: Basic Annals of Qin: In the first year of King Xiaowen, he pardoned offenders, honoured the meritorious servants of the former kings, bestowed generous favour on his kinsmen, and opened the parks and preserves. When King Xiaowen had put off mourning, he came to the throne in October, on the day Jihai; on the third day, Xinchou, he died, and his son King Zhuangxiang was set up.

div.head: Shiji III: Hereditary Houses
div.p: Hereditary House of Zhao: In the sixteenth year, Lian Po besieged Yan. Yue Cheng was made Lord Wuxiang.

div.head: Shiji IV: Biographies
div.p: Biography of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru: Five years after the siege of Handan was raised, Yan adopted Li Fu's plan — "those of Zhao in their prime were all used up at Changping, and their orphans are not yet grown" — and raised troops to strike at Zhao. Zhao sent Lian Po in command; he struck and heavily defeated the Yan army at Hao, killed Li Fu, and went on to besiege Yan. Yan ceded five Fortresses and sued for peace, and this was granted. Zhao enfeoffed Lian Po with Weiwen as Lord Xinping and made him Acting Chancellor of State.

When Lian Po had been dismissed at Changping and returned home, in the time when he had lost his position, his old retainers all left. When he was again employed as general, the retainers came back again. Lian Po said: "Retainers, withdraw!" A retainer said: "Ah! How late you are in seeing it, my lord! All under heaven make their friendships as in the market: when you have position I follow you, and when you have none I leave. That is the plain principle of it; what is there to resent?" After six years, Zhao sent Lian Po to attack Wei's Fanyang, and he took it.

div.head: Shiji V: Biographies
div.p: Biography of Lü Buwei: The King of Qin had been on the throne one year when he died; his posthumous title was Xiaowen. The Heir Apparent, Zichu, succeeded him; this was King Zhuangxiang. The one King Zhuangxiang had as his mother, Queen Huayang, became Queen Dowager Huayang, and his real mother, Lady Xia, was honoured as Queen Dowager Xia.
